name: bitlocker
description: BitLocker bypass & recovery: YellowKey (0-day FsTx WinRE), Bitpixie (CVE-2023-21563), cold boot VMK extraction, TPM SPI sniffing, DMA/PCILeech, AD recovery key extraction, exploit chain generation. Includes cross-compiled Windows exploit tool builds.
author: 0xb0rn3 | oxbv1

optional_dependencies.dislocker: Mount BitLocker volumes — apt install dislocker
optional_dependencies.ldap-utils: AD recovery key extraction — apt install ldap-utils
optional_dependencies.smbclient: Remote SMB deployment — apt install smbclient
optional_dependencies.mingw-w64: Cross-compile Windows exploit tools — pacman -S mingw-w64-gcc

target.description: Target IP (remote operations) or empty for physical

computer.description: Target computer name for AD recovery key lookup

target_drive.description: Drive letter (e.g. E:) for local YellowKey deploy

usb_path.description: Mount point of USB drive for YellowKey payload

efi_path.description: Mount point of EFI partition for YellowKey payload

mem_image.description: Path to memory dump file for cold_boot/dma_pcileech analysis

usb_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for USB insertion (usb_deploy)

usb_index.description: Drive index to select if multiple USBs detected

auto_select.description: Auto-select first detected drive without prompt

operations.survey: Enumerate BitLocker attack surface: applicable techniques ranked by requirements, tool availability, YellowKey payload readiness
operations.usb_deploy: Interactive USB detection loop: waits for USB insertion (like ADB loop in android_pentest), lists detected drives with size/model/label, auto-mounts selected drive, deploys YellowKey FsTx payload to System Volume Information, provides step-by-step trigger instructions
operations.yellowkey: YellowKey (0-day): deploy FsTx payload to USB/EFI partition System Volume Information. SHIFT+Restart+hold CTRL → WinRE SYSTEM shell bypasses BitLocker. Windows 11/Server 2022/2025
operations.yellowkey_remote: Deploy YellowKey FsTx payload remotely via SMB to target Windows machine System Volume Information
operations.bitpixie: CVE-2023-21563 network BitLocker bypass: malicious PXE bootloader captures TPM-released VMK (TPM-only, no PIN, pre-patch)
operations.cold_boot: Cold boot attack: analyze RAM dump for BitLocker VMK (volatility3 bitlocker plugin). Chilling RAM extends retention window
operations.tpm_sniff: TPM SPI bus interception guide: discrete TPM VMK capture via logic analyzer (Saleae/Bus Pirate) during pre-boot
operations.dma_pcileech: DMA attack via PCILeech (Thunderbolt/PCIe): full RAM read/write on running system, extract VMK or patch LSASS
operations.recovery_key_ad: Extract BitLocker recovery keys from AD msFVE-RecoveryInformation objects (domain-joined targets, any domain user)
operations.tool_build: Compile Windows exploit tools (BlueHammer/RedSun/GreenPlasma/UnDefend) via mingw cross-compiler + MiniPlasma via dotnet build
operations.exploit_generate: Generate prioritized BitLocker bypass chain for target profile (OS version, PIN, domain join, network/USB/physical access)
operations.auto: Survey target + generate recommended exploit chain. For USB delivery: use usb_deploy operation

attack_chain: 1. tool_build — cross-compile all Windows exploit tools
4. yellowkey — easiest: FsTx in System Volume Information + SHIFT+Restart+CTRL
5. recovery_key_ad — if domain-joined: read msFVE-RecoveryPassword from AD
6. bitpixie — if network and no PIN: CVE-2023-21563 PXE VMK capture
7. tpm_sniff or dma_pcileech — last resort: hardware attacks
After BitLocker bypass → volume mounted → deploy winadsec operations for full Windows compromise
usb_deploy_quick: # → Insert USB drive into attacker machine
# → 'Payload deployed. Remove USB, insert into target.'
# → SHIFT+Restart+hold CTRL on target → SYSTEM shell
yellowkey_quick: # Then on target: SHIFT+Restart → hold CTRL → SYSTEM shell
notes: YellowKey: WinRE cldflt.sys FsTx component present only in WinRE image — possibly intentional backdoor
YellowKey Windows 11/Server 2022/2025 only — Windows 10 not affected
BitLocker PIN is the strongest mitigation: prevents cold boot AND TPM SPI sniffing
AD recovery keys are often readable by any domain user — first thing to check on domain-joined targets
